title: Unconditional cohomology finiteness across a dense open
statement: Let k be algebraically closed, f:X -> Spec k a reduced curve [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], Λ a finite commutative ring, and F a constructible etale sheaf of Λ-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. For a dense open j:U -> X let G=j_!j^*F [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. All cohomology groups of F are finite if and only if all cohomology groups of G are finite; cohomology is that of the underlying abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]. No prime annihilator or properness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof: the finite stalk product, five-term exact sequence, and remarks (a) and (b)

proof.text: The closed complement of the dense open in the Noetherian curve is zero-dimensional and finite, with residue fields k.

The open-closed sequence 0 -> G -> F -> B -> 0 has B=i_*i^*F. Finite exact direct image and Leray identify its cohomology with that on the finite complement. Constructibility makes H^0(B) finite; the zero-dimensional result annihilates H^q(B) for q>0.

The long exact sequence gives 0 -> H^0(G) -> H^0(F) -> H^0(B) -> H^1(G) -> H^1(F) -> 0, with bijections above degree one. Finite kernel and image give finiteness in either direction in degrees zero and one; use the bijections for higher degrees.

mathlib_searches.query: For a constructible sheaf on a curve, extension by zero across a dense open preserves finiteness of all cohomology groups. A prime-annihilated sheaf is primary for that prime and is zero if primary for another prime or if its annihilator is noninvertible but it has invertible-order torsion.
